newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Baan 1996 net seen more than doubling to $34 mln.
newsitem.headline: Baan 1996 net seen more than doubling to $34 mln.

text.p: Computer software firm Baan will more than double full-year net profit when it reports 1996 results late Tuesday, Dutch analysts said.
Most analysts' forecasts were clustered around the consensus of $34 million, in a relatively narrow range of $32.5 to $36.8 million.
Last year, Baan reported net profit of $15.3 million.
Analysts said they expected few surprises as the company continued to ride the wave of its own success.
"Baan has a good track record. Until now it has always lived up to its promises," said Delta Lloyd's Pieter van Gelder.
Both turnover and net profit were seen growing, with margins set to improve, analysts agreed.
Generale Bank's Marcel Dekker said Baan had good growth prospects as it was active in a rapidly expanding market with what he described as a superior product.
"The ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) market (in which Baan is active) is not just another IT (information technology) segment. It's a league of its own," Dekker said.
The ERP market was seen doubling within the next two to three years, he added.
Ahead of the figures Baan shares were some of the biggest gainers in a falling Amsterdam market.
The shares added almost four percent, trading at 81.10 guilders from Monday's 78.10 guilder close.
"They are driven by more than just a good feeling on the results -- Baan shares are also still benefiting from Salomon's upgrade a couple of days ago," said one dealer.
Reuter surveyed nine Dutch securities houses: Amstgeld, BZW, Delta Lloyd Bank, Generale Bank, Labouchere, Van Lanschot, NIB Strating, Wesselius en Kempen & Co.
